# swc_macros_common::binder - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_macros_common/binder/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example)Example

`_binded_a`, `_binded_b` and `_binded_0` in below example are
`BindedField`.

```
struct S {
    a: u8,
    b: u16,
}
let s = S { a: 0, b: 0 };
match s {
    S {
        a: _binded_a,
        b: _binded_b,
    } => {}
}
enum E {
    V1 { a: u8 },
    V2(u16),
    V3,
}
let e = E::V1 { a: 0 };
match e {
    E::V1 { a: _binded_a } => {}
    E::V2(_binded_0) => {}
    E::V3 => {}
}
```
Adopted from `synstructure`.

## Structs[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structs)

- [Binded](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.BindedField.html)- Field
- Binded field. Note that this struct acts like a binded variable for
`quote!`.
- [Binder](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Binder.html)
- Used to bind whole struct or enum.
- [Variant](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.VariantBinder.html)- Binder
- Variant.

# Group in swc_macros_common::prelude - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_macros_common/prelude/struct.Group.html

`pub struct Group { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A delimited token stream.

A `Group` internally contains a `TokenStream` which is surrounded by
`Delimiter`s.

## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#687)#### pub fn [new](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.new)(delimiter: [Delimiter](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Delimiter.html), stream: [TokenStream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.TokenStream.html)) -> [Group](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Group.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#687)

#### pub fn [new](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.new)(delimiter: [Delimiter](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Delimiter.html), stream: [TokenStream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.TokenStream.html)) -> [Group](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Group.html)

Creates a new `Group` with the given delimiter and token stream.

This constructor will set the span for this group to
`Span::call_site()`. To change the span you can use the `set_span`
method below.

Returns the punctuation used as the delimiter for this group: a set of parentheses, square brackets, or curly braces.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#703)#### pub fn [stream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.stream)(&self) -> [TokenStream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.TokenStream.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#703)

#### pub fn [stream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.stream)(&self) -> [TokenStream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.TokenStream.html)

Returns the `TokenStream` of tokens that are delimited in this `Group`.

Note that the returned token stream does not include the delimiter returned above.

Returns the span for the delimiters of this token stream, spanning the
entire `Group`.

# Literal in swc_macros_common::prelude - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_macros_common/prelude/struct.Literal.html

`pub struct Literal { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A literal string (`"hello"`), byte string (`b"hello"`), character (`'a'`),
byte character (`b'a'`), an integer or floating point number with or without
a suffix (`1`, `1u8`, `2.3`, `2.3f32`).

Boolean literals like `true` and `false` do not belong here, they are
`Ident`s.

## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#1119-1132)#### pub fn [u8_suffixed](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.u8_suffixed)(n: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)) -> [Literal](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Literal.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#1119-1132)

#### pub fn [u8_suffixed](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.u8_suffixed)(n: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)) -> [Literal](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Literal.html)

Creates a new suffixed integer literal with the specified value.

This function will create an integer like `1u32` where the integer
value specified is the first part of the token and the integral is
also suffixed at the end. Literals created from negative numbers may
not survive roundtrips through `TokenStream` or strings and may be
broken into two tokens (`-` and positive literal).

Literals created through this method have the `Span::call_site()`
span by default, which can be configured with the `set_span` method
below.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#1134-1147)#### pub fn [u8_unsuffixed](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.u8_unsuffixed)(n: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)) -> [Literal](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Literal.html)

Creates a new unsuffixed integer literal with the specified value.

This function will create an integer like `1` where the integer
value specified is the first part of the token. No suffix is
specified on this token, meaning that invocations like
`Literal::i8_unsuffixed(1)` are equivalent to
`Literal::u32_unsuffixed(1)`. Literals created from negative numbers
may not survive roundtrips through `TokenStream` or strings and may
be broken into two tokens (`-` and positive literal).

Literals created through this method have the `Span::call_site()`
span by default, which can be configured with the `set_span` method
below.

`Literal::u32_unsuffixed(1)`. Literals created from negative numbers
may not survive roundtrips through `TokenStream` or strings and may
be broken into two tokens (`-` and positive literal).

Literals created through this method have the `Span::call_site()`
span by default, which can be configured with the `set_span` method
below.

Creates a new unsuffixed floating-point literal.

This constructor is similar to those like `Literal::i8_unsuffixed` where
the float’s value is emitted directly into the token but no suffix is
used, so it may be inferred to be a `f64` later in the compiler.
Literals created from negative numbers may not survive round-trips
through `TokenStream` or strings and may be broken into two tokens (`-`
and positive literal).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics)Panics

This function requires that the specified float is finite, for example if it is infinity or NaN this function will panic.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#1180)#### pub fn [f64_suffixed](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.f64_suffixed)(f: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)) -> [Literal](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Literal.html)

Creates a new suffixed floating-point literal.

This constructor will create a literal like `1.0f64` where the value
specified is the preceding part of the token and `f64` is the suffix of
the token. This token will always be inferred to be an `f64` in the
compiler. Literals created from negative numbers may not survive
round-trips through `TokenStream` or strings and may be broken into two
tokens (`-` and positive literal).

This function requires that the specified float is finite, for example if it is infinity or NaN this function will panic.

# Punct in swc_macros_common::prelude - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_macros_common/prelude/struct.Punct.html

`pub struct Punct { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A `Punct` is a single punctuation character like `+`, `-` or `#`.

Multicharacter operators like `+=` are represented as two instances of
`Punct` with different forms of `Spacing` returned.

## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

Creates a new `Punct` from the given character and spacing.

The `ch` argument must be a valid punctuation character permitted by the
language, otherwise the function will panic.

The returned `Punct` will have the default span of `Span::call_site()`
which can be further configured with the `set_span` method below.

Returns the spacing of this punctuation character, indicating whether
it’s immediately followed by another `Punct` in the token stream, so
they can potentially be combined into a multicharacter operator
(`Joint`), or it’s followed by some other token or whitespace (`Alone`)
so the operator has certainly ended.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#trait-implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0.106/src/syn/token.rs.html#181)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#impl-Token-for-Punct)

## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#synthetic-implementations)

### impl<T, P> [Punctuated](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Punctuated.html)<T, P>

Determines whether this punctuated sequence is empty, meaning it contains no syntax tree nodes or punctuation.

Returns the number of syntax tree nodes in this punctuated sequence.

This is the number of nodes of type `T`, not counting the punctuation of
type `P`.

Mutably borrows the first element in this sequence.

Mutably borrows the last element in this sequence.

Mutably borrows the element at the given index.

Returns an iterator over borrowed syntax tree nodes of type `&T`.

Returns an iterator over mutably borrowed syntax tree nodes of type
`&mut T`.

Returns an iterator over the contents of this sequence as borrowed punctuated pairs.

Returns an iterator over the contents of this sequence as mutably borrowed punctuated pairs.

Parses one or more occurrences of `T` separated by punctuation of type
`P`, not accepting trailing punctuation.

Parsing continues as long as punctuation `P` is present at the head of
the stream. This method returns upon parsing a `T` and observing that it
is not followed by a `P`, even if there are remaining tokens in the
stream.

# Span in swc_macros_common::prelude - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_macros_common/prelude/struct.Span.html

`pub struct Span { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A region of source code, along with macro expansion information.

## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

The span of the invocation of the current procedural macro.

Identifiers created with this span will be resolved as if they were written directly at the macro call location (call-site hygiene) and other code at the macro call site will be able to refer to them as well.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#375)#### pub fn [mixed_site](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.mixed_site)() -> [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#375)

#### pub fn [mixed_site](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.mixed_site)() -> [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)

The span located at the invocation of the procedural macro, but with
local variables, labels, and `$crate` resolved at the definition site
of the macro. This is the same hygiene behavior as `macro_rules`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#390)#### pub fn [resolved_at](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.resolved_at)(&self, other: [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)) -> [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#390)

#### pub fn [resolved_at](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.resolved_at)(&self, other: [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)) -> [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)

Creates a new span with the same line/column information as `self` but
that resolves symbols as though it were at `other`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#396)#### pub fn [located_at](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.located_at)(&self, other: [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)) -> [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#396)

#### pub fn [located_at](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.located_at)(&self, other: [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)) -> [Span](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Span.html)

Creates a new span with the same name resolution behavior as `self` but
with the line/column information of `other`.

Convert `proc_macro2::Span` to `proc_macro::Span`.

This method is available when building with a nightly compiler, or when
building with rustc 1.29+ *without* semver exempt features.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics)Panics

Panics if called from outside of a procedural macro. Unlike
`proc_macro2::Span`, the `proc_macro::Span` type can only exist within
the context of a procedural macro invocation.

Create a new span encompassing `self` and `other`.

Returns `None` if `self` and `other` are from different files.

Warning: the underlying [ proc_macro::Span::join](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Span.html#method.join) method is
nightly-only. When called from within a procedural macro not using a
nightly compiler, this method will always return

`None`.[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#521)#### pub fn [source_text](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.source_text)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#521)

#### pub fn [source_text](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.source_text)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

Returns the source text behind a span. This preserves the original source code, including spaces and comments. It only returns a result if the span corresponds to real source code.

Note: The observable result of a macro should only rely on the tokens and not on this source text. The result of this function is a best effort to be used for diagnostics only.

# TokenStream in swc_macros_common::prelude - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_macros_common/prelude/struct.TokenStream.html

`pub struct TokenStream { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An abstract stream of tokens, or more concretely a sequence of token trees.

This type provides interfaces for iterating over token trees and for collecting token trees into one stream.

Token stream is both the input and output of `#[proc_macro]`,
`#[proc_macro_attribute]` and `#[proc_macro_derive]` definitions.

## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

## Trait Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#trait-implementations)

`TokenStream::default()` returns an empty stream,
i.e. this is equivalent with `TokenStream::new()`.

Attempts to break the string into tokens and parse those tokens into a token stream.

May fail for a number of reasons, for example, if the string contains unbalanced delimiters or characters not existing in the language.

NOTE: Some errors may cause panics instead of returning `LexError`. We
reserve the right to change these errors into `LexError`s later.

# Delimiter in swc_macros_common::prelude - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_macros_common/prelude/enum.Delimiter.html

```
pub enum Delimiter {
    Parenthesis,
    Brace,
    Bracket,
    None,
}
```
## Expand description

Describes how a sequence of token trees is delimited.

## Variants[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#variants)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#variant.Parenthesis)

### Parenthesis

`( ... )`

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#variant.Brace)

### Brace

`{ ... }`

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#variant.Bracket)

### Bracket

`[ ... ]`

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#variant.None)

### None

`∅ ... ∅`

An invisible delimiter, that may, for example, appear around tokens
coming from a “macro variable” `$var`. It is important to preserve
operator priorities in cases like `$var * 3` where `$var` is `1 + 2`.
Invisible delimiters may not survive roundtrip of a token stream through
a string.

Note: rustc currently can ignore the grouping of tokens delimited by `None` in the output
of a proc_macro. Only `None`-delimited groups created by a macro_rules macro in the input
of a proc_macro macro are preserved, and only in very specific circumstances.
Any `None`-delimited groups (re)created by a proc_macro will therefore not preserve
operator priorities as indicated above. The other `Delimiter` variants should be used
instead in this context. This is a rustc bug. For details, see
[rust-lang/rust#67062](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/67062).

## Trait Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#trait-implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#641)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#impl-Copy-for-Delimiter)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#641)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#impl-Eq-for-Delimiter)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#641)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#impl-StructuralPartialEq-for-Delimiter)

### impl [StructuralPartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.StructuralPartialEq.html) for [Delimiter](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Delimiter.html)

## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#synthetic-implementations)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#impl-Freeze-for-Delimiter)

# Enum Element

[Source](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0.106/src/syn/punctuated.rs.html#951) ```
pub enum Element<T, P> {
    Punctuated(T, P),
    End(T),
}
```

## Expand description

A single syntax tree node of type `T` followed by its trailing punctuation
of type `P` if any.

Refer to the [module documentation](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0.106/syn/punctuated/index.html) for details about punctuated sequences.

Extracts the syntax tree node from this punctuated pair, discarding the
following punctuation.

Borrows the syntax tree node from this punctuated pair.

Mutably borrows the syntax tree node from this punctuated pair.

Borrows the punctuation from this punctuated pair, unless this pair is
the final one and there is no trailing punctuation.

Mutably borrows the punctuation from this punctuated pair, unless the
pair is the final one and there is no trailing punctuation.

[§](#example)Example

```
punctuated.insert(0, parse_quote!('lifetime));
if let Some(punct) = punctuated.pairs_mut().next().unwrap().punct_mut() {
    punct.span = span;
}
```

Creates a punctuated pair out of a syntax tree node and an optional
following punctuation.

Produces this punctuated pair as a tuple of syntax tree node and
optional following punctuation.

## Required Methods[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/src/quote/to_tokens.rs.html#50)#### fn [to_tokens](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#tymethod.to_tokens)(&self, tokens: &mut [TokenStream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.TokenStream.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/src/quote/to_tokens.rs.html#50)

#### fn [to_tokens](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#tymethod.to_tokens)(&self, tokens: &mut [TokenStream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.TokenStream.html))

Write `self` to the given `TokenStream`.

The token append methods provided by the [ TokenStreamExt](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/quote/ext/trait.TokenStreamExt.html) extension
trait may be useful for implementing

`ToTokens`.[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example)Example

Example implementation for a struct representing Rust paths like
`std::cmp::PartialEq`:

```
use proc_macro2::{TokenTree, Spacing, Span, Punct, TokenStream};
use quote::{TokenStreamExt, ToTokens};
pub struct Path {
    pub global: bool,
    pub segments: Vec<PathSegment>,
}
impl ToTokens for Path {
    fn to_tokens(&self, tokens: &mut TokenStream) {
        for (i, segment) in self.segments.iter().enumerate() {
            if i > 0 || self.global {
                // Double colon `::`
                tokens.append(Punct::new(':', Spacing::Joint));
                tokens.append(Punct::new(':', Spacing::Alone));
            }
            segment.to_tokens(tokens);
        }
    }
}
```
## Provided Methods[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#provided-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/src/quote/to_tokens.rs.html#56)#### fn [to_token_stream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.to_token_stream)(&self) -> [TokenStream](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.TokenStream.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/src/quote/to_tokens.rs.html#56)

Convert `self` directly into a `TokenStream` object.

This method is implicitly implemented using `to_tokens`, and acts as a
convenience method for consumers of the `ToTokens` trait.

# swc_macros_common/binder.rs

[1](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#1)//! # Example
[2](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#2)//!
[3](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#3)//! `_binded_a`, `_binded_b` and `_binded_0` in below example are
[4](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#4)//! `BindedField`.
[5](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#5)//!
[6](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#6)//! ```rust
[7](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#7)//! struct S {
[8](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#8)//!     a: u8,
[9](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#9)//!     b: u16,
[10](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#10)//! }
[11](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#11)//! let s = S { a: 0, b: 0 };
[12](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#12)//! match s {
[13](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#13)//!     S {
[14](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#14)//!         a: _binded_a,
[15](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#15)//!         b: _binded_b,
[16](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#16)//!     } => {}
[17](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#17)//! }
[18](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#18)//! enum E {
[19](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#19)//!     V1 { a: u8 },
[20](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#20)//!     V2(u16),
[21](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#21)//!     V3,
[22](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#22)//! }
[23](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#23)//! let e = E::V1 { a: 0 };
[24](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#24)//! match e {
[25](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#25)//!     E::V1 { a: _binded_a } => {}
[26](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#26)//!     E::V2(_binded_0) => {}
[27](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#27)//!     E::V3 => {}
[28](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#28)//! }
[29](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#29)//! ```

[119](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#119)    /// `EnumName::VariantName` for enum, and `StructName` for struct.
[120](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#120)    pub fn qual_path(&self) -> Path {
[121](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#121)        match self.enum_name {
[122](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#122)            Some(enum_name) => {
[123](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#123)                let vn = &self.name;
[124](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#124)
[125](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#125)                parse_quote!(#enum_name::#vn)
[126](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#126)            }
[127](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#127)            None => self.name.clone().into(),
[128](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#128)        }

[131](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#131)    ///

[135](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#135)        prefix: &str,

[139](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#139)        let path = self.qual_path();
[140](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#140)
[141](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#141)        let (pat, bindings) = match *self.data {
[142](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#142)            Fields::Unit => {
[143](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#143)                // EnumName::VariantName
[144](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#144)                let pat = Pat::Path(PatPath {
[145](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#145)                    qself: None,
[146](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#146)                    path,
[147](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#147)                    attrs: Default::default(),
[148](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#148)                });
[149](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#149)
[150](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#150)                // Unit struct does not have any field to bind
[151](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#151)                (pat, Vec::new())
[152](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#152)            }
[153](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#153)            Fields::Named(FieldsNamed {
[154](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#154)                named: ref fields,
[155](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#155)                brace_token,
[156](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#156)            }) => {
[157](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#157)                let mut bindings = Vec::new();
[158](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#158)
[159](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#159)                let fields = fields
[160](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#160)                    .pairs()
[161](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#161)                    .map(|e| {
[162](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#162)                        let (t, p) = e.into_tuple();
[163](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#163)                        Pair::new(t, p.cloned())
[164](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#164)                    })
[165](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#165)                    .enumerate()
[166](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#166)                    .map(|(idx, f)| {
[167](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#167)                        f.map_item(|f| {
[168](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#168)                            let ident = f
[169](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#169)                                .ident
[170](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#170)                                .clone()
[171](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#171)                                .expect("field of struct-like variants should have name");
[172](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#172)
[173](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#173)                            let binded_ident =
[174](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#174)                                Ident::new(&format!("{prefix}{ident}"), ident.span());
[175](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#175)                            bindings.push(BindedField {
[176](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#176)                                idx,
[177](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#177)                                binded_ident: binded_ident.clone(),
[178](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#178)                                field: f,
[179](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#179)                            });
[180](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#180)                            FieldPat {
[181](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#181)                                attrs: f
[182](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#182)                                    .attrs
[183](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#183)                                    .iter()
[184](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#184)                                    .filter(|attr| is_attr_name(attr, "cfg"))
[185](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#185)                                    .cloned()
[186](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#186)                                    .collect(),
[187](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#187)                                colon_token: f.colon_token,
[188](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#188)                                member: Member::Named(ident),
[189](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#189)                                pat: Box::new(Pat::Ident(PatIdent {
[190](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#190)                                    by_ref,
[191](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#191)                                    mutability,
[192](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#192)                                    ident: binded_ident,
[193](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#193)                                    subpat: None,
[194](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#194)                                    attrs: Default::default(),
[195](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#195)                                })),
[196](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#196)                            }
[197](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#197)                        })
[198](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#198)                    })
[199](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#199)                    .collect();
[200](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#200)                // EnumName::VariantName { fields }
[201](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#201)                let pat = Pat::Struct(PatStruct {
[202](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#202)                    attrs: Default::default(),
[203](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#203)                    qself: None,
[204](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#204)                    path,
[205](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#205)                    brace_token,
[206](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#206)                    fields,
[207](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#207)                    rest: None,
[208](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#208)                });
[209](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#209)                (pat, bindings)
[210](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#210)            }
[211](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#211)            Fields::Unnamed(FieldsUnnamed {
[212](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#212)                unnamed: ref fields,
[213](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#213)                paren_token,
[214](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#214)            }) => {
[215](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#215)                // TODO
[216](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#216)                let mut bindings = Vec::new();
[217](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#217)
[218](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#218)                let pats = fields
[219](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#219)                    .pairs()
[220](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#220)                    .map(|e| {
[221](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#221)                        let (t, p) = e.into_tuple();
[222](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#222)                        Pair::new(t, p.cloned())
[223](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#223)                    })
[224](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#224)                    .enumerate()

[226](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#226)                        f.map_item(|f| {

[228](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#228)
[229](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#229)                            bindings.push(BindedField {
[230](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#230)                                idx,
[231](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#231)                                binded_ident: binded_ident.clone(),
[232](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#232)                                field: f,
[233](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#233)                            });
[234](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#234)
[235](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#235)                            Pat::Ident(PatIdent {

[254](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#254)            }
[255](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#255)        };
[256](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#256)
[257](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#257)        // if we don't need to move fields, we should match on reference to make tuple

[259](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#259)
[260](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#260)        // let pat = match by_ref {

[269](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#269)        (pat, bindings)
[270](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#270)    }

[273](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#273)/// Binded field. Note that this struct acts like a binded variable for
[274](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#274)/// `quote!`.
[275](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#275)#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
[276](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#276)pub struct BindedField<'a> {

[278](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#278)    idx: usize,
[279](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#279)    field: &'a Field,
[280](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#280)}

[285](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#285)    }

[290](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#290)    }

[19](#19)    pub fn new(input: &'a DeriveInput) -> Self {
[20](#20)        let (generics, self_ty) = {
[21](#21)            let params = input
[23](#23)                .generics
[24](#24)                .params
[25](#25)                .clone()
[26](#26)                .into_pairs()
[27](#27)                .map(|mut pair| {
[28](#28)                    if let GenericParam::Type(ref mut t) = *pair.value_mut() {
[29](#29)                        t.eq_token = None;
[30](#30)                        t.default = None;
[31](#31)                    }
[32](#32)
[33](#33)                    pair
[34](#34)                })
[35](#35)                .collect();
[36](#36)
[37](#37)            let generics = Generics {
[38](#38)                params,
[39](#39)                gt_token: input.generics.gt_token,
[40](#40)                lt_token: input.generics.lt_token,
[41](#41)                where_clause: input.generics.where_clause.clone(),
[42](#42)            };
[43](#43)
[44](#44)            let ty: Box<Type> = {
[46](#46)                let (_, ty_generics, _) = input.generics.split_for_impl();
[47](#47)                let mut t = TokenStream::new();
[48](#48)                input.ident.to_tokens(&mut t);
[49](#49)                ty_generics.to_tokens(&mut t);
[50](#50)                Box::new(
[51](#51)                    parse2(t.into_token_stream())
[52](#52)                        .unwrap_or_else(|err| panic!("failed to parse type: {err}")),
[53](#53)                )
[54](#54)            };
[55](#55)
[56](#56)            (generics, ty)
[57](#57)        };
[58](#58)
[59](#59)        Derive {
[60](#60)            input,
[61](#61)            out: ItemImpl {
[62](#62)                attrs: Vec::new(),
[63](#63)                impl_token: Token!(impl)(def_site()),
[64](#64)                brace_token: Default::default(),
[65](#65)                defaultness: None,
[66](#66)                unsafety: None,
[67](#67)                generics,
[68](#68)                trait_: None,
[69](#69)                self_ty,
[70](#70)                items: Default::default(),
[71](#71)            },
[72](#72)        }
[73](#73)    }
[74](#74)

[89](#89)    pub fn append_to(mut self, item: ItemImpl) -> ItemImpl {
[90](#90)        assert_eq!(self.out.trait_, None);
[91](#91)        if !self.out.generics.params.empty_or_trailing() {
[92](#92)            self.out.generics.params.push_punct(Token![,](def_site()));
[93](#93)        }
[94](#94)
[95](#95)        self.out
[96](#96)            .generics
[97](#97)            .params
[98](#98)            .extend(item.generics.params.into_pairs());
[99](#99)

generics.rs[1](#1)use std::collections::BTreeSet;

[8](#8)impl<'a> Derive<'a> {
[9](#9)    pub fn all_generic_fields(&self) -> Vec<&'a Field> {
[10](#10)        struct TypeVisitor<'a> {
[11](#11)            params: &'a BTreeSet<Ident>,
[12](#12)            is_generic: bool,
[13](#13)        }
[14](#14)
[15](#15)        impl Visit<'_> for TypeVisitor<'_> {
[16](#16)            fn visit_path(&mut self, path: &Path) {
[17](#17)                if let Some(seg) = path.segments.last() {
[18](#18)                    if seg.ident == "PhantomData" {
[19](#19)                        return;
[22](#22)                    }
[23](#23)                }
[24](#24)
[25](#25)                if path.leading_colon.is_none() {
[26](#26)                    if let Some(seg) = path.segments.first() {
[27](#27)                        let id = &seg.ident;
[28](#28)                        if self.params.contains(id) {
[29](#29)                            self.is_generic = true;
[30](#30)                        }
[31](#31)                    }
[32](#32)                }
[33](#33)
[34](#34)                visit::visit_path(self, path)
[35](#35)            }
[36](#36)
[37](#37)            fn visit_macro(&mut self, _: &Macro) {}
[38](#38)        }
[39](#39)
[40](#40)        struct FieldVisitor<'a> {
[41](#41)            params: BTreeSet<Ident>,
[43](#43)            fields: Vec<&'a Field>,
[44](#44)        }
[45](#45)
[46](#46)        impl<'a: 'b, 'b> Visit<'a> for FieldVisitor<'b> {
[47](#47)            fn visit_field(&mut self, field: &'a Field) {
[48](#48)                let mut vis = TypeVisitor {
[49](#49)                    params: &self.params,
[50](#50)                    is_generic: false,
[51](#51)                };
[52](#52)                vis.visit_type(&field.ty);
[53](#53)                if vis.is_generic {
[54](#54)                    self.fields.push(field);
[55](#55)                }
[56](#56)            }
[57](#57)        }
[58](#58)
[59](#59)        let mut vis = FieldVisitor {
[60](#60)            params: self
[61](#61)                .input
[62](#62)                .generics
[63](#63)                .params
[64](#64)                .iter()
[65](#65)                .filter_map(|p| match *p {
[66](#66)                    GenericParam::Type(TypeParam { ref ident, .. }) => Some(ident.clone()),
[67](#67)                    _ => None,
[68](#68)                })
[69](#69)                .collect(),
[70](#70)            fields: Vec::new(),
[71](#71)        };
[72](#72)
[73](#73)        vis.visit_derive_input(self.input);
[74](#74)        vis.fields
[75](#75)    }
[76](#76)
[77](#77)    pub fn add_where_predicates<I>(&mut self, preds: I)
[78](#78)    where
[79](#79)        I: IntoIterator<Item = WherePredicate>,
[80](#80)    {
[81](#81)        let preds = preds
[82](#82)            .into_iter()
[83](#83)            .map(|t| Pair::Punctuated(t, Token![,](def_site())));
[84](#84)
[85](#85)        match self.out.generics.where_clause {
[86](#86)            Some(WhereClause {
[87](#87)                ref mut predicates, ..
[88](#88)            }) => {
[89](#89)                if !predicates.empty_or_trailing() {
[90](#90)                    predicates.push_punct(Token![,](def_site()));
[91](#91)                }
[92](#92)
[93](#93)                predicates.extend(preds)
[94](#94)            }
[95](#95)            None => {
[96](#96)                self.out.generics.where_clause = Some(WhereClause {
[97](#97)                    where_token: Token![where](def_site()),
[98](#98)                    predicates: preds.collect(),
[99](#99)                })
[100](#100)            }
[101](#101)        }
[102](#102)    }
[103](#103)
[104](#104)    pub fn bound_self(&mut self, trait_: Path) {
[106](#106)        let self_ty: Type = parse(quote!(Self).into()).unwrap();
[107](#107)
[108](#108)        let bound = WherePredicate::Type(PredicateType {
[109](#109)            lifetimes: None,
[110](#110)            bounded_ty: self_ty,
[111](#111)            colon_token: Token![:](def_site()),
[112](#112)            bounds: iter::once(Pair::End(TypeParamBound::Trait(TraitBound {
[114](#114)                modifier: TraitBoundModifier::None,
[115](#115)                lifetimes: None,
[116](#116)                path: trait_,
[117](#117)                paren_token: None,
[118](#118)            })))
[119](#119)            .collect(),
[120](#120)        });
[121](#121)
[122](#122)        self.add_where_predicates(iter::once(bound))
[123](#123)    }

# swc_macros_common/syn_ext.rs

[1](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#1)use quote::quote;
[2](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#2)use syn::{punctuated::Pair, *};
[3](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#3)
[4](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#4)use crate::def_site;
[5](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#5)
[6](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#6)/// Extension trait for `ItemImpl` (impl block).
[7](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#7)pub trait ItemImplExt {
[8](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#8)    /// Instead of
[9](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#9)    ///
[10](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#10)    /// ```rust,ignore
[11](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#11)    /// let (impl_generics, ty_generics, where_clause) = input.generics.split_for_impl();
[12](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#12)    ///
[13](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#13)    /// let item: Item = Quote::new(def_site::<Span>())
[14](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#14)    ///     .quote_with(smart_quote!(
[15](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#15)    /// Vars {
[16](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#16)    /// Type: type_name,
[17](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#17)    /// impl_generics,
[18](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#18)    /// ty_generics,
[19](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#19)    /// where_clause,
[20](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#20)    /// },
[21](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#21)    /// {
[22](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#22)    /// impl impl_generics ::swc_common::AstNode for Type ty_generics
[23](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#23)    /// where_clause {}
[24](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#24)    /// }
[25](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#25)    /// )).parse();
[26](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#26)    /// ```
[27](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#27)    ///
[28](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#28)    /// You can use this like
[29](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#29)    ///
[30](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#30)    /// ```rust,ignore
[31](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#31)    // let item = Quote::new(def_site::<Span>())
[32](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#32)    ///     .quote_with(smart_quote!(Vars { Type: type_name }, {
[33](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#33)    ///         impl ::swc_common::AstNode for Type {}
[34](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#34)    ///     }))
[35](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#35)    ///     .parse::<ItemImpl>()
[36](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#36)    ///     .with_generics(input.generics);
[37](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#37)    /// ```
[38](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#38)    fn with_generics(self, generics: Generics) -> Self;
[39](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#39)}

[41](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#41)impl ItemImplExt for ItemImpl {
[42](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#42)    fn with_generics(mut self, mut generics: Generics) -> Self {
[43](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#43)        // TODO: Check conflicting name
[44](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#44)
[45](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#45)        let need_new_punct = !generics.params.empty_or_trailing();
[46](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#46)        if need_new_punct {
[47](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#47)            generics.params.push_punct(Token![,](def_site()));
[48](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#48)        }
[49](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#49)
[50](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#50)        // Respan
[51](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#51)        if let Some(t) = generics.lt_token {
[52](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#52)            self.generics.lt_token = Some(t)
[53](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#53)        }
[54](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#54)        if let Some(t) = generics.gt_token {
[55](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#55)            self.generics.gt_token = Some(t)
[56](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#56)        }
[57](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#57)
[58](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#58)        let ty = self.self_ty;
[59](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#59)
[60](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#60)        // Handle generics defined on struct, enum, or union.
[61](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#61)        let mut item: ItemImpl = {
[62](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#62)            let (_, ty_generics, _) = generics.split_for_impl();
[63](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#63)            let item = quote! {
[64](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#64)                #ty #ty_generics
[65](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#65)            };
[66](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#66)
[67](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#67)            ItemImpl {
[68](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#68)                generics,
[69](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#69)                self_ty: parse2(item).unwrap(),
[70](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#70)                ..self
[71](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#71)            }
[72](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#72)        };
[73](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#73)
[74](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#74)        // Handle generics added by proc-macro.
[75](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#75)        item.generics
[76](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#76)            .params
[77](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#77)            .extend(self.generics.params.into_pairs());
[78](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#78)
[79](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#79)        item
[80](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#80)    }

[83](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#83)pub trait PairExt<T, P>: Sized + Into<Pair<T, P>> {
[84](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#84)    fn map_item<F, NewItem>(self, op: F) -> Pair<NewItem, P>
[85](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#85)    where
[86](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#86)        F: FnOnce(T) -> NewItem,
[87](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#87)    {
[88](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#88)        match self.into() {
[89](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#89)            Pair::Punctuated(t, p) => Pair::Punctuated(op(t), p),
[90](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#90)            Pair::End(t) => Pair::End(op(t)),
[91](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#91)        }
[92](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#92)    }
[93](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#93)}
